atlantic.fact: The Atlantic Ocean is the second-largest ocean on Earth, covering approximately 82.4 million square kilometers.
The Atlantic Ocean is home to the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, an underwater mountain range that stretches about 16,000 kilometers.
The deepest point in the Atlantic Ocean is the Milwaukee Deep in the Puerto Rico Trench, at approximately 8,600 meters.
The Atlantic Ocean contains about 20% of the world's ocean water.
The Atlantic Ocean separates Europe and Africa from North and South America.
The Atlantic Ocean is home to diverse marine life including whales, dolphins, sharks, and numerous fish species.
The North Atlantic Gyre is a major oceanic circulation pattern that creates the famous Sargasso Sea.
The Atlantic Ocean receives water from major rivers including the Amazon, Congo, Mississippi, and St. Lawrence.

pacific.fact: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth, covering approximately 165.2 million square kilometers.
The Pacific Ocean is almost as large as all other oceans combined.
The Mariana Trench, located in the Pacific Ocean, is the deepest known part of any ocean at approximately 10,994 meters.
The Pacific Ocean is home to the Ring of Fire, a region of intense volcanic and seismic activity.
The Pacific Ocean contains about 46% of the world's ocean water.
The Pacific Ocean is home to diverse marine life including whales, sharks, sea turtles, and countless fish species.
The Pacific Ocean separates Asia and Australia from North and South America.
The Great Barrier Reef, located in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Australia, is the world's largest coral reef system.
The Pacific Ocean has major currents including the Kuroshio Current and the California Current that influence global climate.
The Pacific Ocean was named by Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan in the 16th century.
